candidates.teaser: There's a creature on Earth that scientists say genuinely cannot die of old age — and it lives in the ocean.
candidates.video_title: The Only Animal That Can't Die of Old Age
candidates.video_description: The jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii can reverse its own aging process and return to its juvenile state — indefinitely. Scientists call it the only known biologically immortal animal on Earth.
candidates.script: This jellyfish discovered in the Mediterranean in 1883 cannot die of old age — ever. When it gets sick or old, it does something no other animal on Earth can do: it shrinks back into a baby and starts its entire life over. Scientists call it biologically immortal. It can repeat this cycle indefinitely. The real question isn't how it does it — it's why we haven't figured out how to make us do the same.

candidates.teaser: There's a 600-year-old book that the world's best codebreakers, linguists, and AI have all failed to read.
candidates.video_description: The Voynich Manuscript is a 240-page illustrated book written in an unknown script that has never been decoded. NSA cryptographers, World War II codebreakers, and modern AI have all failed to crack it.
candidates.script: The NSA — the agency that cracked Nazi codes — spent decades trying to read this book and gave up. The Voynich Manuscript, written around 1420, is 240 pages of unknown language, strange plant drawings, and astronomical charts. No alphabet on Earth matches its script. Modern AI analyzed every pattern and still found nothing. Either it's the most elaborate hoax in history — or someone buried a secret so deep no one has ever touched it.

candidates.teaser: There's an animal alive right now that has survived every mass extinction on Earth — including the one that wiped out the dinosaurs.
candidates.video_title: The Animal That Survived Every Extinction
candidates.video_description: Tardigrades are microscopic animals that have survived all five of Earth's mass extinctions. They can endure the vacuum of space, radiation 1,000 times lethal to humans, and temperatures from -272°C to 150°C.
candidates.script: Something is living on your roof right now that survived every single mass extinction on Earth — including the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs. It's called a tardigrade, and it's less than 1 millimeter long. Send it into the vacuum of space — it survives. Hit it with radiation 1,000 times the lethal human dose — it survives. Freeze it to -272 degrees — it wakes back up. Whatever ends life on Earth, scientists say this thing will probably outlive it.

candidates.topic: The Library of Alexandria — what was actually lost
candidates.teaser: Everyone knows the Library of Alexandria burned — but almost nobody knows what was actually inside it when it did.
candidates.video_description: The Library of Alexandria held an estimated 400,000 to 700,000 scrolls — including works on surgery, astronomy, and mathematics that took humanity over 1,000 years to rediscover after they were lost.
candidates.script: When the Library of Alexandria burned, we didn't just lose books. We lost surgical techniques that took medicine 1,400 years to rediscover. We lost star maps accurate enough to rival modern telescopes. We lost up to 700,000 scrolls — most of them the only copies on Earth. Some historians believe the Industrial Revolution could have happened in the year 500 AD if that library had survived. Think about what world we'd be living in right now.

candidates.topic: The Pando tree — world's largest single organism (by mass)
candidates.teaser: There's a single living organism in Utah that is 80,000 years old and covers 43 hectares — and it's slowly dying.
candidates.video_title: One Organism, 80,000 Years Old — Dying Now
candidates.video_description: Pando is a colony of quaking aspen trees in Utah that share a single root system, making them one organism. Weighing 6 million kilograms and spanning 43 hectares, it is the largest known organism on Earth by mass — and it is shrinking.
candidates.script: What looks like a forest in Utah is actually a single living organism — one root system, one genetic code, 47,000 trunks. It's called Pando, it weighs 6 million kilograms, and it's been alive for at least 80,000 years. It watched the woolly mammoths go extinct. It was already ancient when the pyramids were built. And right now, for the first time in 80 millennia, it is dying — because of us. Does that make you feel anything?
